newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Shell Sri Lanka strike hits industry.
newsitem.headline: Shell Sri Lanka strike hits industry.

text.p: A four-day strike at Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, owned by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, is threatening to shut down industries that use liquid petroleum gas (LPG), officials said on Tuesday.

"We have been forced to curtail production by about 60 percent due to the strike," said Shirley Gurusinghe, general manager of Ceylon Glass Company, which has an average daily capacity of about 275,000 bottles.
"Our LPG supplies will run out by tomorrow and we will be down to zero production if this strike doesn't end today," Gurusinghe told Reuters.
Talks between striking trade union leaders, company and government officials failed to produce results on Tuesday, Labour Commissioner R. Wimalasena told Reuters.
"We could not come to a settlement today. But we hope to have another round of talks on Thursday," said Wimalasena, who is mediating between the two sides.
Officials for Shell Gas Lanka were not immediately available for comment.

The strike was launched last Friday by workers of the All Ceylon Commercial and Industrial Workers Union demanding an immediate halt to transfers of employees and the reinstatement of six workers who were dismissed.
The company's outlets which supply gas to domestic consumers had already put up shutters and thousands of consumers could run out of gas in a few days, independent distributors said.
Several industries faced the threat of closing down as their LPG stocks dwindled four days into the strike.
An official for Dankotuwa Procelain, a leading manufacturer of porcelainware, said the company may have to shut down one of its two kilns if the strike continues.

"We have a two-week LPG storage, which is already down by four days," the official said. "At the moment, our production is going on as usual, but in another two days we will have to take precautionary action."
A ship with 1,750 tonnes of gas has been waiting outside Colombo port since Saturday, unable to unload because of the strike.
This is the second strike at the company since it was privatised in October 1995.

A six-day strike by union labour, demanding the reinstatement of nine workers suspended for violating safety rules at Colombo port when unloading gas, brought gas distribution to a halt in the Indian Ocean island last November.
